findings.title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the logged-in user has no `topic_users` row for the topic, and the next line calls `tu.notification_level` on it. That raises NoMethodError and the page returns a 500. The URL is a plain GET, so any logged-in user can reach it for a topic they never visited, for example by following a forwarded email link from another account. Handle nil, either with `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row, or by returning a clean error.

findings.title: Unsubscribe toggle is not idempotent: reloading the page mutes the topic
findings.body: The first visit drops a watching or tracking user to regular. Any later hit on the same URL, whether a page reload, a double click, or an email-client or security-scanner prefetch, sees `notification_level <= regular` and mutes the topic. A user who only asked to stop watching can end up with the topic fully muted. The resulting state depends on how many times the URL is requested, not on user intent. The action should be idempotent, or require explicit confirmation before escalating to muted.

findings.title: State-changing action exposed on GET (CSRF / prefetch)
findings.body: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` map to an action that writes `topic_users.notification_level`. GET requests are not covered by CSRF protection. A post or any third-party page that embeds an image or link pointing at `/t/x/<id>/unsubscribe` will change the notification level for any logged-in viewer. Link prefetchers and scanners trigger it too. The write should be a POST/PUT from the client page (with a CSRF token) after the user confirms, rather than a side effect of loading the page.

findings.title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping and MessageBus
findings.body: The notification level is set by assigning the attribute and calling `tu.save!`. Everywhere else it is changed through `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (to `user_changed`) and publishes `notification_level_change` on MessageBus. Here the reason stays at its old value, the timestamp is not updated, and other open tabs are not told about the change. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` to keep behaviour consistent.

findings.title: add_unsubscribe_link now silently requires an unsubscribe_url option
findings.body: The English `unsubscribe_link` string now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) interpolate it from `template_args` with no default. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`, including plugins and other mailers, will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when the email is built. The spec had to be edited to pass `unsubscribe_url` to avoid this. Provide a fallback in `template_args`, or only include the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

findings.title: Template name likely does not match the topicUnsubscribe route
findings.body: The route is declared as `topicUnsubscribe` and the controller, view and route files are all named `topic-unsubscribe`, but the template lives at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, so its name is `topic/unsubscribe`. The Discourse resolver looks up `topicUnsubscribe`, `topic_unsubscribe` and `topic-unsubscribe`, not `topic/unsubscribe`. If it does not resolve, the unsubscribe page renders empty and shows neither the message nor the notification dropdown. Rename the file to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`, or verify that the resolver finds the nested path.

findings.title: New unsubscribe feature has no tests
findings.body: The only spec change is adding `unsubscribe_url` to an existing fixture so it stops raising. Nothing asserts that the per-topic URL appears in the email body or HTML part. There is no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, covering downgrade to regular, escalation to muted, the slug redirect, the missing-TopicUser case and the not-logged-in case. There is no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`. The behaviour problems above (nil TopicUser, non-idempotent toggle) would have been caught by basic controller tests.
